first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly matching the documented durable lift from signup simplification (memory_31) and shortened onboarding (memory_86). This is the most evidence-backed lever available and addresses a metric actually in decline, supporting sustainable long-term qualified revenue rather than short-term acquisition. Promotional pricing is tempting given competitor entry pricing, but memory_73 explicitly warns it boosts acquisition/revenue short-term while materially harming 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a strategy — pursuing it now would trade long-term qualified revenue for a reactive short-term response, contrary to the stated objective. I verify memory_31 to confirm the onboarding evidence is solid before committing the week's only experiment slot to it, and memory_73 to double-check the retention-harm finding still holds before ruling out pricing as an option, since competitive pressure raises the temptation to override that caution. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist are viable but don't address the specific metrics currently declining, and activation messaging is a reasonable alternative but onboarding has a more direct causal link to the completion-rate drop and a slightly stronger evidentiary base (two corroborating memories).
